aum.basis: Menlo Ventures reports through TWO exempt reporting advisers, neither of them an SEC- or state-registered investment adviser, so no Item 5.F regulatory AUM exists for either. The sworn substitute is Schedule D Section 7.B.(1): MENLO VENTURES MANAGEMENT, L.P. (CRD 283999, SEC 802-108043, annual amendment 2026-03-31) reports 31 private funds at $10,774,945,953 of current gross asset value, and MV MANAGEMENT XI, LLC (CRD 161248, SEC 802-75435, annual amendment 2026-04-01) reports 8 funds — the X, XI and XII vintages and their co-invest siblings — at $967,805,151. The two filings are one day apart, so the composite of $11,742,751,104 across 39 funds is coherent as of one fiscal year end. BOTH RANGE ENDS ARE THAT SWORN NUMBER and it is a FLOOR: the firm announced $3 billion of new capital on 2026-06-23, after both amendments were filed, and no press 'AUM' figure above the sworn composite was found.

funds.basis: 45 of the firm's own vehicles filed 52 Form Ds; the table lists the flagship ladder, the growth family, the thematic sleeves and the two dedicated Anthropic vehicles, and counts rather than lists the co-invest and employee funds (Menlo Entrepreneurs Fund IX/IX-A/X/XII/XIV/XVI and Inflection, Menlo CxO Fund XVI and Inflection III, Menlo XV Innovators, XVII Innovators and Private Investors, Inflection IV Innovators and Private Investors, MMEF X-XV, MM Inflection, MMSOP) and the single-deal SPVs (Suno Partners I/II, Atlas Partners, Cybersecurity Partners, ABN AI Partners, Axm Partners, LV Partners). FILING STYLE: Menlo files the fund's full target as the total-offering amount and amends `sold` at close, so every size here is the sworn offering, and the $0-sold cross-check the Accel run relied on does not apply. THREE FUND-LADDER FINDINGS: there is no Menlo Ventures XIII anywhere in the record; the Special Opportunities family was RENAMED Inflection between the Form Ds (SOF I/II/III) and the 2026 ADV (Inflection I/II/III), which is why the same vehicles appear under two names; and the Olympus fund is registered on EDGAR as 'Menlo Olympic Fund I' and in the ADV as 'MENLO OLYMPUS FUND I'.

investment_stage.basis: The firm's own description of its two funds: 'Menlo Ventures XVII invests from Seed to Series A' and 'Menlo Inflection IV provides growth capital at Series B and beyond'. Pre-Seed is added on the Anthology Fund's own stated floor ('first investment (Pre-Seed)', cheques from $100,000) and is corroborated by the landed base, where 4 rows carry a Pre-Seed entry and 56 a Seed entry.

investment_geo.basis: Derived from the landed base: 563 of 596 rows are US (94.5%), and 320 of 596 sit in the San Francisco Bay Area. The non-US tail is thin and scattered — GB 7, IL 6, SE 4, DE 3, CA 2, and one each in IN, CN, TR and AU — so the core is US alone and the two-label cap is not reached. SF Bay Area is carried as 'other' because it is a sub-geography of the core rather than a second market.

investment_scope.basis: Generalist, and the base says so unusually clearly: no single sector reaches 18% of the book. Recomputed off the grind's own focus column over all 596 rows — Data Infrastructure 106, Healthcare & Bio 82, Industrial & Robotics 72, Consumer & Marketplaces 72, SaaS 54, Security 53, Fintech & Payments 50, Media/Gaming/Advertising 50, AI & Applied AI 26, DevTools & APIs 23, with Crypto & Web3 and Climate & Energy at 4 each and below the publication floor. The shape is a fifty-year book read at once: the networking, storage and semiconductor heritage still outweighs the AI wave the firm is now all-in on, because focus records what a company DOES and not when it was bought.

investment_range.basis: Three legs, per COLLECTION.md 11. MEDIAN $15.0M: the partner-anchored entry round across the 109 verified members whose entry filing carries an amount (p25 $7.0M, p75 $28.2M) — a round-size proxy for cheque size, fair for a lead investor and flagged as such. LOWER LIMIT $100,000: the Anthology Fund's own published floor ('investments starting at $100,000 and up'), the smallest cheque the firm states it writes. UPPER LIMIT $1,000,000,000: the combined $500M + $500M total offerings of Menlo Inflection AI Partners and Menlo Inflection AI Investors, both filed 2024-01-09 for the Anthropic Series D the firm calls 'the largest check we'd ever written'. The 10-15% single-position concentration cross-check does NOT bind here and is recorded as not binding: that position was funded through dedicated single-company vehicles rather than out of the flagship, which is the structure the cross-check assumes.

history.value: Menlo Ventures was founded on Sand Hill Road in 1976 by H. DuBose Montgomery and is one of the oldest venture firms still investing. It backed Gilead, Hotmail, Uber, Roku, Siri and Warby Parker, and led Anthropic's $750M Series D in 2024. For its fiftieth anniversary in 2026 it announced $3B of new funds.
history.basis: The firm's own 50th-anniversary post supplies the founding, the Anthropic sequence and the $3B raise; every company named is a member row in the landed base, and the 1970s-1990s names come from the firm's own archived sector and Prior Investments pages (1998-2007). Rewritten to the reader-facing shape (PRO-147, 2026-09-24). The two-fund ladder (Menlo Ventures XVII for seed and Series A, Menlo Inflection IV for growth), the entry-round shares from the firm's portfolio pages, the single-company Anthropic vehicles and the $100M Anthology Fund are in the basis above.

investment_concept.basis: The firm's own statement, verbatim from its homepage headline (h1), read 2026-09-26; sentence case, straight quotes and a closing period are the only edits.
